original_question: Construct a homomorphism of a subgroup of a Golod group(see 9.76) onto an infinite AT-group as defined in(A. V. Rozhkov, Math. Notes, 40, no. 5(1986), 827–836). Cf. 13.55
target_in_paper: Problem 21.131 in the section "New Problems (21st Issue, 2026)": construct a homomorphism from a subgroup of a Golod group onto an infinite AT-group, with an explicit cross-reference to Problem 13.55.
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact target problem in the paper almost verbatim. In particular, it correctly asks for a homomorphism from a subgroup of a Golod group, not from the whole Golod group, and it correctly requires the image to be an infinite AT-group. It also correctly preserves the paper's cross-reference to 13.55.
missing_details: The draft does not spell out the paper's internal definition of a Golod group from Problem 9.76.

To make the question stand-alone, one should specify that a Golod group is a group G = <1 + x1 + I, 1 + x2 + I, ..., 1 + xr + I> contained in the adjoint group 1 + F/I, where r >= 2, F is the free algebra of polynomials without constant terms in noncommuting variables x1, ..., xr over a field of characteristic p > 0, and I is an ideal such that F/I is a non-nilpotent nil-algebra.
It should be explicit that the task is to exhibit a subgroup H <= G and a surjective homomorphism H ↠ A onto an infinite AT-group A.

The paper itself does not define AT-group internally; it only refers to Rozhkov's 1986 paper for that definition, so a paper-faithful stand-alone restatement must retain the phrase 'AT-group in the sense of Rozhkov'.
The reference 'Cf. 13.55' should not be folded into the main statement: 13.55 is a related stronger problem asking whether a Golod group itself can be isomorphic to an AT-group.
refined_question: Construct explicitly a subgroup H of a Golod group G = <1 + x1 + I, 1 + x2 + I, ..., 1 + xr + I> <= 1 + F/I, where r >= 2, F is the free algebra of polynomials without constant terms in noncommuting variables x1, ..., xr over a field of characteristic p > 0, and I is an ideal such that F/I is a non-nilpotent nil-algebra, together with a surjective homomorphism H ↠ A onto an infinite AT-group A in the sense of A. V. Rozhkov (Math. Notes 40 (1986), no. 5, 827-836).
justification: The draft is aiming at Problem 21.131, not merely at the earlier Problem 13.55. This is clear because 21.131 uses exactly the formulation 'Construct a homomorphism of a subgroup of a Golod group ... onto an infinite AT-group' and then explicitly adds 'Cf. 13.55'. Problem 9.76 is the place where the paper defines 'Golod group', so that definition must be imported to make the question self-contained. By contrast, the paper does not restate the definition of AT-group, only citing Rozhkov's paper, so the most faithful refinement is to preserve that external reference rather than broaden or reinterpret the notion.
